subject: Billing & payment paths for Hosted API — monthly invoicing vs card and net terms
messages:

Cc: procurement@fintechco.com
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API billing options & PO process

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — connection looked great. Procurement wants a short write-up of our billing options so we can choose a path for the pilot. Specifically they asked: 1) can we pay by card or do you offer monthly invoicing, 2) if invoicing is available what are the standard net terms (Net 30/45/60), 3) what do you need from our side to issue POs (tax ID, billing contact, MSA?), and 4) do you have a standard rate card for the hosted API (baseline rates + any volume tiers).

We want to keep the pilot simple but may need an invoice path for internal chargeback. Can you send the rate card and a short summary of steps for procurement?

—Jane
Jane Howell
VP, Platform Strategy | FintechCo
procurement@fintechco.com

From: jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API billing options & PO process

Hi Jane — great to meet you too. Short answers up front: yes, we support both card and monthly invoicing; standard invoice terms are Net 30 for self-serve/credit-approved customers, Net 45 available by request for larger committed contracts; and we can accept POs — we typically need a copy of the PO, billing/legal contact, tax ID (W-9 for US), and an executed MSA for invoiced accounts.

Attached is our hosted API rate card (baseline, unit pricing by token tier) and a one‑page procurement checklist to share with your finance team. Highlights:
- Baseline hosted costs: $0.012 / 1k tokens for generation (baseline medium model); embedding pricing and large-model tiers are listed on page 2.
- Volume tiers: automated discounts at 10M+ tokens and 100M+ tokens; committed discounts handled via deal terms.
- Card payments are enabled immediately after signup; invoices require billing setup and credit review (2–5 business days).

If you want pricing locked for the pilot period we can add a 90‑day price commitment via a simple order form. If procurement prefers invoice + Net 30 we can route this through our billing ops team (I’ll need the PO and billing contact).

Attaching: Redwood_hosted_ratecard_2026.pdf, Redwood_procurement_checklist_2026.pdf

Next steps I recommend: 1) Procurement reviews the checklist, 2) you share any PO template, 3) we pull together a short order form if a commitment/discount is requested.

Best,

Also tagging procurement here (procurement@fintechco.com) — they prefer monthly invoicing tied to POs for internal chargeback.

From: jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: FintechCo billing questions — quick internal

Folks — copying the ask from FintechCo above. Quick thoughts before I reply to procurement:

1) VAT: we issue invoices from our EMEA subsidiary when required and include VAT handling per the customer's billing entity. Operations can confirm the exact VAT flow, but standard approach is to invoice the local entity and apply local tax rules.

2) Discount/credits: FintechCo is a strategic prospect with potential expansion across multiple teams. I propose offering a pilot package: 20% off hosted baseline pricing for the first 6 months OR $15K promotional credit (whichever is better for their structure). This would require approval from Sales Ops for entitlement configuration and official signoff from Sales Leadership on discount depth.

3) PO process: We can accept POs; we'll need a signed MSA or order form. For a short pilot we could do a simple order form (no full legal redlines) to speed procurement.

Can we get Sales Ops to pre-approve 20% for pilot deals under $50K so we don't need to escalate on every small pilot? If not, what's the current approval flow/time?

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call if easier.

—Jasmine

Subject: Re: Fwd: FintechCo billing questions — quick internal

Jasmine — I like the 20% pilot discount or fixed credit option. A couple notes:
- Approvals: Sales Ops can pre-authorize up to 15% without leadership signoff; anything >15% will need signoff from the regional sales lead (I can route that). For $50K or less, a 20% discount is borderline but achievable if we make it a time-limited pilot and tie it to a usage commit.
- Billing ops: we should confirm VAT handling with finance — if they're billing an EU legal entity, we should issue with VAT per country rules; if it's a US entity with EU ops, VAT likely not applied.
- Doc flow: suggest we prepare a one‑page order form and an MSA stub (non-redline) and route via DocuSign. Procurement teams like a clear PO-to-invoice mapping.

If you want, I can pre-approve 20% for this specific deal (DEAL-1453) contingent on Jasmine getting a signed order form and confirmation of the commit.

—Jonas

Proposed pilot terms (quick win):
- Billing path: monthly invoicing tied to a PO (you indicated preference for internal chargeback).
- Payment terms: Net 30 on invoices.
- Promo: 20% off baseline hosted API rates for the first 6 months OR $15,000 promotional credit (customer choice).
- Commit: no long-term lock — pilot capped at $50K list spend over 6 months to qualify for the promo.
- VAT: we will invoice the entity you specify; if the billed entity is in the EU we will apply VAT per local rules (Finance will confirm).

Required from FintechCo to proceed: PO (PDF), billing contact + tax ID (W-9 if US), and confirmation of which promo you prefer. Once we have that we’ll send a short order form + MSA stub for signature and route invoices monthly.
